Real Termux plugins now run inside one shared supervisor (Termux local or a single proot container). The container is started once and kept alive while the app is open, so later plugin starts skip the proot initialization overhead.

Keep the shared supervisor (and proot container) alive even when this app is killed in the background, so the next plugin start is instant. Uses battery-optimization exemption, a notification, and Shizuku/Dhizuku privileges when available.

UIN Tool was denied the com.termux.permission.RUN_COMMAND permission (declared by Termux, not UIN Tool). Open the Termux app: Termux Settings -> "Allow external apps" / "Run commands", then retry.

To run commands in Real Termux, UIN Tool needs the "com.termux.permission.RUN_COMMAND" permission.

This permission is declared by the Termux app itself, not by UIN Tool, so grant it from inside Termux:
1. Open the Termux app.
2. Long-press the terminal area -> More -> Allow external apps (or Termux Settings -> Allow external apps).
3. Confirm "Allow run commands" when prompted, then return and retry.

Also make sure "allow-external-apps=true" is set in ~/.termux/termux.properties.

Fill in the plugin basic configuration

Here is a brief introduction to each field:

• Plugin ID: unique identifier, in reversed domain format, e.g. com.example.myplugin, immutable after creation.
• Plugin Name: display name, e.g. My Plugin.
• Author: developer name.
• Description: brief functionality description.
• Version Code / Version Name: integer code and readable version for updates.
• Main Class: entry point class for native plugins, must include the package.
• Entry File: the script/class loaded at startup.
• Plugin Notice: description shown in the plugin list.
• Permissions: permissions the plugin declares, shown to the user before enabling.
• Dependencies: comma-separated plugin IDs this plugin relies on.
• Min Host Version / API Level: minimum host version and Android API level required.
• Category: plugin category.
• Update URL: remote address for plugin update checks.
• Backend (web + backend): start command, keep-alive, timeout, health check path.
• Resource limits: max memory / CPU time / concurrent tasks (reserved, not enforced).
• External content (openWith): share-menu / open-with receiver for text, links and files.
